candidates.title: Baby storytime and rhyme time at a Plateau public library branch
candidates.description: Montreal's public library network usually offers short baby sessions with songs, rhymes and books for infants and their caregivers. It is a gentle, free outing that suits a newborn and is a good way to meet other parents. Category: library, ongoing, newborn fit.
candidates.coverageNote: General knowledge: the library network reliably runs baby sessions, but I can't confirm which branch, schedule or registration rules. Check the Montreal libraries listings. Language of sessions (French or English) varies.

candidates.title: Stroller walks in Parc La Fontaine
candidates.description: A large, central park with flat paths, shade and ponds, suited to daily fresh-air walks with a newborn in a carrier or stroller. It is free and needs no registration. Category: outdoor, ongoing, newborn fit.
candidates.coverageNote: General knowledge: the park is well known and open year-round. Winter paths can be icy, so conditions vary with the season.

They are useful for newborn-stage parents looking for company. Category: drop_in, ongoing, newborn fit.
candidates.coverageNote: General knowledge: such organizations commonly exist in central Montreal boroughs, but I can't name a specific one or confirm its hours, fees or age range for newborns.

candidates.title: CLSC perinatal and breastfeeding support or baby weigh-in
candidates.description: Quebec's local CLSC health centres typically offer post-natal follow-up, infant weight checks, breastfeeding help and parent information groups. These are practical, low-pressure ways to get support in the early weeks. Category: program, ongoing, newborn fit.
